# Implementation Plan: Plugin Scope — top-level | subagent | both

*Generated by `/plan-with-ralph` on 2026-05-26. Refined 2026-05-25 with Option A (subagent-config-time filter at `build_agent_shared_config`) per `plans/plugin-scope-agents-redesign-brainstorm.md` §3. Ready for `/implement-with-ralph --from-plan <job_dir>/plan.md`.*

## Operator Amendments (2026-05-25 — Option A redesign)

After post-plan-review feasibility brainstorm (`plans/plugin-scope-agents-redesign-brainstorm.md`), the operator adopted **Option A**: subagent-config-time filter via override-layer injection at `core/src/tools/handlers/multi_agents_common.rs::build_agent_shared_config`. This block supersedes the prior 2026-05-26 amendments and the original "thread `PluginLoadContext` everywhere" plan body. **Where this block and the plan body disagree, this block wins.**

- **Single-seam scope filter.** All subagent `Config` objects are constructed via `build_agent_shared_config` (`core/src/tools/handlers/multi_agents_common.rs:225`). The Option A filter is a 3-to-5 line edit calling `codex_plugin_scope::apply_subagent_plugin_filter(&mut config)` AFTER `apply_spawn_agent_runtime_overrides`. The filter synthesizes a high-precedence override `ConfigLayerStack` layer containing `[plugins.<id>] enabled = false` entries for every plugin whose manifest declares `scope.agent: "top-level"`. The existing `PluginsManager::plugins_for_config()` cache key (`version_for_toml(effective_config())`) naturally differs for the subagent's layer stack, so the manager remains untouched and top-level/subagent results coexist in cache.
- **No signature threading.** The original plan added a new `PluginLoadContext` parameter to `plugins_for_config()` and every caller (22 call sites across 14 files) plus `to_mcp_config()` (5 callers). **All of that threading is removed.** Manager / Config / Session / Connectors / MCP / Skills-watcher / TUI background requests / app-server processors / chatgpt connectors all stay untouched.
- **Field shape — NESTED, not flat.** Manifest uses `scope: { agent: "top-level" | "subagent" | "both" }`, NOT a flat `scope.agent` key. Forward-compatible with Phase 2c's planned `scope: { host, agent }` axis. The overlay parser:
  - Reads `manifest.scope.agent` (nested).
  - Tolerates a missing `scope` object entirely (defaults to `scope.agent = Both`).
  - Tolerates a present `scope` object with missing `agent` (defaults to `Both`).
  - **Refuses to load on unknown `scope.agent` values** (per F-012; no silent broadening, no silent narrowing).
- **Default `Both`.** Plugins without explicit `scope.agent` continue to load in both contexts.
- **Defer cross-repo ralph-orchestration manifest update.** Ship the codex-side gate + local test fixture only. Cross-repo PR to `ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/ralph-orchestration/.codex-plugin/plugin.json` is a follow-up; log in `plans/codexu-roadmap.md`.
- **Reuse Happy daemon trust model.** No new `HAPPY_ALLOW_AGENT_SPAWN` env var. Daemon's existing same-machine/same-user trust + `agent-spawner` role being operator-declared is sufficient gating.
- **Phase 2c host/agent axis out of scope.** Documented-only in roadmap.
- **Manifest cache lifecycle = process-lifetime.** The overlay's manifest re-parser caches parsed `.codex-plugin/plugin.json` results in a `static Lazy<RwLock<HashMap<PathBuf, ManifestEntry>>>` for the codex process lifetime. No mtime invalidation, no cache-clear hook. Matches today's plugin-cache semantics (operators reinstall to refresh). Cost: 1 disk read per configured plugin (typically <10) on first subagent spawn; <1 ms per subagent spawn after warm.
- **`build_agent_shared_config` is exhaustive.** Verified via `git grep` against pinned submodule: the four call sites in `agent_jobs.rs:130`, `multi_agents/spawn.rs:84`, `multi_agents_v2/spawn.rs:83`, and `multi_agents/resume_agent.rs:171` all funnel through `build_agent_spawn_config` → `build_agent_shared_config` (or `build_agent_resume_config` → `build_agent_shared_config`). Implementer MUST re-run this grep at implementation time as a US-002 acceptance check.

**Text-substitution rule (for the rest of this plan and all generated PRD/story criteria):** read every occurrence of `scope.agent` in flat-key form as the nested `scope: { agent: ... }` shape. Test fixtures, manifest examples, parser code, and all acceptance criteria use the nested form.

## Overview

Codex's plugin manifest gains a new orthogonal scope axis: `scope.agent ∈ { top-level, subagent, both }`. Plugins declared as `top-level` are visible only to top-level operator sessions; plugins declared as `subagent` are visible only to spawned subagent sessions; `both` (the default) preserves today's behavior for backward compatibility. A new built-in `agent-spawner` role + tool lets a constrained subagent ask the operator's Happy daemon to spawn a top-level session, without going through codex's `spawn_agent` (which would produce a SubAgent session that cannot see top-level-only plugins).

> **Note (F-005 — scope.agent='subagent' enforcement deferred):** The `scope.agent = "subagent"` value is parsed and accepted by the overlay and the predicate correctly models `PluginScope::Subagent`. However, top-level enforcement (hiding subagent-only plugins from top-level Config construction) is **not yet implemented**. Today a `scope.agent = "subagent"` plugin will still load in top-level sessions. When `apply_subagent_plugin_filter` encounters a `Subagent`-scoped plugin it emits a one-time `tracing::warn!` per plugin id (dedup via process-lifetime `Mutex<HashSet>`): *"scope.agent='subagent' is parsed but not yet enforced for top-level sessions; track as future work. Plugin: <id>"*. Full top-level enforcement requires a symmetric filter callsite at the top-level `Config::load` path — a larger seam analysis deferred to a follow-up task tracked in `plans/codexu-roadmap.md`.

The implementation lives in a new overlay crate `codex/codex-rs-overlay/codex-plugin-scope/` plus a single-seam filter call at `core/src/tools/handlers/multi_agents_common.rs::build_agent_shared_config` (marked `// SANDBOX PATCH: plugin-scope-axis`). The upstream manifest schema at `codex/external/repos/codex-patched/codex-rs/core-plugins/src/manifest.rs` is NOT modified — the overlay crate re-reads `.codex-plugin/plugin.json` independently. **`PluginsManager::plugins_for_config()` is not modified and its signature is not changed.** The filter operates by mutating the subagent's `Config::config_layer_stack` to push an override layer that disables top-level-only plugins; the existing manager naturally observes the new layer stack via its cache key.

### Technical Constraints

- **Upstream `manifest.rs` is read-only.** The overlay crate must independently parse the new field from `<plugin_root>/.codex-plugin/plugin.json`.
- **Phase 2c host/agent scope is NOT shipping yet.** Research confirms this is documented in `plans/codexu-roadmap.md` but not in code. This plan implements only the new `scope.agent` axis; host/agent stays out of scope.
- **Plugin cache stays context-blind by design.** Scope filtering happens BEFORE the manager sees the subagent's Config — by mutating the layer stack at `build_agent_shared_config`. The manager naturally produces a different cache key for the subagent's layer stack.
- **Rust does not build locally on this Windows workstation.** Daily iteration relies on CI (`codex/.github/workflows/invariant-check.yml`) — "CI green is the source of truth" replaces "cargo build green" for Rust ACs.
- **Marketplace plugin source edits do NOT propagate to cached installed plugins.** The ralph-orchestration plugin manifest lives in `gim-home/ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/ralph-orchestration/` (a separate repo). Editing it cross-repo is deferred; this job ships the codex-side gate + a local-plugin test fixture proving the gate works.
- **`SessionSource::restriction_product()`** is insufficient — it returns `None` for subagents and currently gates product compatibility, not agent visibility. Tool-exposure gating classifies on `SessionSource::SubAgent(_)` directly.
- **Override-layer precedence must beat user/project layer.** The overlay's synthetic disable layer is pushed AFTER any user-level `[plugins.x] enabled = true`. The implementer must add an explicit test (US-002 AC): parent config has `enabled = true` for a top-level-only plugin → subagent override layer wins → subagent's effective config disables the plugin.
- **Manifest re-parser cache lifetime = process-lifetime.** `static Lazy<RwLock<HashMap<PathBuf, ManifestEntry>>>` in the overlay crate. Cost is one disk read per configured plugin on first subagent spawn after process start; warm-cache cost is one HashMap lookup. No invalidation on plugin reinstall — operator restarts the codex process to refresh (matches today's plugin-cache semantics).

## Approach

### Architecture

**Two-layer split:**

1. **Overlay crate `codex-plugin-scope` (NEW):**
   - Owns the `PluginScope` enum: `TopLevel`, `Subagent`, `Both`.
   - Owns the `PluginLoadContext` enum: `TopLevel`, `Subagent`. (Internal to the overlay; not threaded through upstream.)
   - Owns the predicate `PluginScope::allows(&self, ctx: PluginLoadContext) -> bool`.
   - Owns the manifest re-parser that opens `<plugin_root>/.codex-plugin/plugin.json` independently and extracts the new nested `scope: { agent: ... }` field with serde-permissive parsing. Default = `Both` on missing `scope` / missing `agent`. **Refuses to load on unknown `agent` values.**
   - Owns the process-lifetime cache: `static Lazy<RwLock<HashMap<PathBuf, ManifestEntry>>>`, keyed by canonical plugin install path.
   - Owns the public entrypoint `apply_subagent_plugin_filter(&mut Config)`:
     1. Reads `config.config_layer_stack.effective_config()` to enumerate the configured `[plugins.*]` entries (already in scope from upstream Config).
     2. For each configured plugin, resolves its install path via the same convention used by `core-plugins/src/loader.rs` (overlay-side helper, not a new upstream call).
     3. Re-reads `.codex-plugin/plugin.json` from the install path (cached) and extracts `scope.agent`.
     4. If `scope.agent == TopLevel`, accumulates the plugin id into the synthetic override TOML.
     5. Builds a one-shot override `ConfigLayerEntry` containing `[plugins.<id>] enabled = false` for each top-level-only plugin.
     6. Calls `config.config_layer_stack.with_user_layer(synthetic_layer)` (or equivalent) and reassigns `config.config_layer_stack`.
     7. No-op when no top-level plugins are configured (single HashMap lookup, no layer push).

2. **Minimal upstream seams (each marked `// SANDBOX PATCH: plugin-scope-axis`):**
   - `core/src/tools/handlers/multi_agents_common.rs`: add the 3-to-5 line call `codex_plugin_scope::apply_subagent_plugin_filter(&mut config)` inside `build_agent_shared_config`, AFTER `apply_spawn_agent_runtime_overrides`. **This is the only seam that performs scope filtering.**
   - `core/src/agent/role.rs`: register `agent-spawner` as a built-in role.
   - `tools/src/tool_config.rs`: gate `spawn_top_level_session` exposure on `SessionSource::SubAgent(... agent_role: Some("agent-spawner") ...)`. Gate `spawn_agent` exposure on `TopLevel` context (so subagents cannot spawn further subagents, per the seed's explicit constraint).
   - `core/src/tools/spec_plan.rs`: register `spawn_top_level_session` as a native function tool when enabled; gate `spawn_agent` registration on top-level context.
   - `core/src/tools/handlers/mod.rs`: re-export the new handler.
   - `core/src/tools/handlers/spawn_top_level_session.rs` (NEW upstream file): handler that posts to the Happy daemon HTTP control endpoint.
   - `core/src/tools/handlers/multi_agents/spawn.rs`: defensive reject for v1 `spawn_agent` from subagent context + unit test.
   - `core/src/tools/handlers/multi_agents_v2/spawn.rs`: defensive reject for v2 `spawn_agent` from subagent context + unit test.

3. **agent-spawner tool transport:**
   - A built-in Rust-native Codex function tool `spawn_top_level_session` available only when `turn.session_source` is `SessionSource::SubAgent(SubAgentSource::ThreadSpawn { agent_role: Some("agent-spawner"), .. })`; `tools/src/tool_config.rs` controls exposure and the handler defensively enforces the same check from the current `TurnContext`.
   - Tool's implementation posts to the local Happy daemon HTTP control endpoint `/spawn-session-from-session`, which reuses the existing daemon `spawnSessionFromSession` implementation registered today as the machine RPC `spawn-session-from-session`. This produces a top-level Happy session that can load top-level-only plugins. Do NOT route this through the Happy MCP bridge: `runCodex.ts` only configures the session-wide bridge, and `happyMcpStdioBridge.ts` / `startHappyServer.ts` expose only `change_title` with no per-subagent role context.
   - HTTP contract: `POST /spawn-session-from-session` with body `{ parentSessionId: string, config: { agent: "claude" | "codex" | "gemini" | "openclaw", path?: string, model?: string, permissionMode?: string, effortLevel?: string, initialMessage?: string } }`. `parentSessionId` is a bare local Happy session id only (`1..128`, `[A-Za-z0-9_-]`, no `machineId:` prefix). Response body is the existing `SpawnSessionResult` shape constrained to `{ type: "success", sessionId: string } | { type: "error", errorMessage: string }`; daemon-side directory-approval requests are converted to `type: "error"` by `spawnSessionFromSession`.
   - The handler obtains `parentSessionId` from `HAPPY_CURRENT_SESSION_ID`, injected by `packages/happy-cli/src/codex/runCodex.ts` when launching `codex app-server`, and posts to `HAPPY_DAEMON_CONTROL_URL`. `HAPPY_CURRENT_SESSION_ID` is `session.sessionId` / `response.id`, the bare local Happy session id expected by `apiMachine.ts` validation, not Codex's `conversation_id` or a composite `machineId:sessionId`. Missing env or daemon URL returns a structured tool error.
   - Authorization gate: operator must enable the capability via Happy daemon env / config (out-of-band) — already the trust model for the existing daemon RPC. No new opt-in env var needed beyond the session identity/control URL plumbing above.

### Implementation Strategy (ordered)

1. **Scaffold `codex-plugin-scope` overlay crate** with `Cargo.toml`, `src/lib.rs` re-exports, `src/parser.rs` (manifest re-reader + process-lifetime cache), `src/context.rs` (`PluginLoadContext` enum), `src/predicate.rs` (`PluginScope` enum + `allows()`), `src/filter.rs` (`apply_subagent_plugin_filter(&mut Config)`). Add unit tests covering: (a) parser tolerates missing `scope`; (b) parser tolerates missing `scope.agent`; (c) parser refuses unknown `scope.agent` values; (d) override-layer synthesis is empty when no plugins are configured; (e) override-layer synthesis disables the right plugin ids; (f) process-lifetime cache is hit on repeated calls. Register in workspace `Cargo.toml` as both a workspace member and a `[workspace.dependencies]` entry; add `codex-plugin-scope = { workspace = true }` to `core/Cargo.toml` (the only consuming crate); refresh `Cargo.lock`.
2. **Wire the single-seam filter** at `core/src/tools/handlers/multi_agents_common.rs::build_agent_shared_config`. Add `// SANDBOX PATCH: plugin-scope-axis` marker + the 3-to-5 line `codex_plugin_scope::apply_subagent_plugin_filter(&mut config)` call AFTER `apply_spawn_agent_runtime_overrides`. Re-run `git grep -n 'config.clone()'` inside `core/src/tools/handlers/multi_agents*` and `core/src/tools/handlers/agent_jobs.rs` to confirm `build_agent_shared_config` (and its sibling `build_agent_resume_config` → `build_agent_shared_config`) remain the exhaustive Config-from-parent-Config seams; document the grep in the story log. Add an integration test in `core/src/tools/handlers/multi_agents_tests.rs`: spawn an agent with a parent Config that enables a top-level-only test plugin; assert `child.config_layer_stack.effective_config()` shows that plugin disabled. Include a precedence-stress variant: parent config sets `[plugins.x] enabled = true`; subagent override layer wins → effective config has `enabled = false`.
3. **Register `agent-spawner` role** in `core/src/agent/role.rs`. Add a concrete unit test against `agent::role` enumeration that includes `"agent-spawner"` with a non-empty description (F-016).
4. **Implement `spawn_top_level_session` Rust-native tool handler** — define Rust request/response structs matching the HTTP contract above, gate exposure in `tools/src/tool_config.rs`, register the handler in `core/src/tools/handlers/mod.rs` + `core/src/tools/spec_plan.rs`, and implement `core/src/tools/handlers/spawn_top_level_session.rs` using `reqwest` to POST to `HAPPY_DAEMON_CONTROL_URL` with `parentSessionId` from `HAPPY_CURRENT_SESSION_ID`.
5. **Gate `spawn_agent` exposure for subagents** in `tool_config.rs` + `core/src/tools/spec_plan.rs`, and add handler-side defensive rejects in both spawn paths: `core/src/tools/handlers/multi_agents/spawn.rs` and `core/src/tools/handlers/multi_agents_v2/spawn.rs` (a helper in `multi_agents_common.rs` is OK only if both handlers call it). Add a unit test covering the reject path in each handler module. **Must land co-resident with step 3+4** (F-017): no in-flight commit may leave subagents able to call `spawn_agent` while role/tool work is mid-flight.
6. **TypeScript daemon/control wiring (happy-cli):**
    - Add a local daemon HTTP `/spawn-session-from-session` route in `packages/happy-cli/src/daemon/controlServer.ts` that implements the contract defined above, and thread the existing `spawnSessionFromSessionHandler` from `packages/happy-cli/src/daemon/run.ts` into it, reusing the bare-local-`parentSessionId` validation shape from `packages/happy-cli/src/api/apiMachine.ts`.
    - Extend `packages/happy-cli/src/codex/codexAppServerClient.ts` to accept explicit extra child env, and have `packages/happy-cli/src/codex/runCodex.ts` pass `HAPPY_CURRENT_SESSION_ID=session.sessionId` (the bare local Happy session id, matching `response.id` for a created/resumed session) plus `HAPPY_DAEMON_CONTROL_URL` derived from daemon state when available.
    - Leave `packages/happy-cli/src/codex/happyMcpStdioBridge.ts` and `packages/happy-cli/src/claude/utils/startHappyServer.ts` unchanged; those are the existing `change_title` MCP bridge/server only, and `spawn_top_level_session` must stay Rust-native + daemon HTTP.
    - Add vitest coverage for the control endpoint and for `runCodex`/`CodexAppServerClient` env injection.
7. **Add fork-side invariant test** in `codex-rs-overlay/codex-invariant-tests/tests/plugin_scope_filtering.rs` — `include_str!()` source-pattern assertion that the `// SANDBOX PATCH: plugin-scope-axis` marker exists in `core/src/tools/handlers/multi_agents_common.rs` AND in the role/tool registration files (`agent/role.rs`, `tool_config.rs`, `spec_plan.rs`, `multi_agents/spawn.rs`, `multi_agents_v2/spawn.rs`). Also assert (source-pattern grep) that `multi_agents_common.rs::build_agent_shared_config` calls `codex_plugin_scope::apply_subagent_plugin_filter` — this catches accidental removal of the filter call during rebase.
8. **Add local-fixture plugin manifests:**
   - `packages/codexu-plugin/.codex-plugin/plugin.json` — declare `scope.agent: "both"` explicitly for documentation purposes; do NOT change visibility (F-013 mandate: codexu-plugin stays at `"both"`).
   - A second test-fixture plugin (e.g., `codex/external/repos/codex-patched/codex-rs/core/src/tools/handlers/multi_agents_tests/fixtures/top_level_only_plugin/.codex-plugin/plugin.json`) declares `scope.agent: "top-level"` so the integration test in step 2 has a real on-disk plugin manifest to load. Test-only path; no marketplace integration.
9. **Cross-package typecheck** — `pnpm -r typecheck` green across happy-cli/happy-server/happy-app/happy-wire.
10. **Push to topic branch + CI verify** — Rust CI in `codex/.github/workflows/invariant-check.yml` must go green. Verify Cargo metadata is in sync (`Cargo.lock` updated). Bazel BUILD verification: the workspace addition is just one new crate consumed only by `core`; check whether the `core/BUILD.bazel` Cargo-derived deps need updating; if `codex_rust_crate` macro auto-derives from `Cargo.toml`, no edit is required. Update only when the invariant test or CI fails on Bazel metadata.

## Scope

### In Scope
- New `scope: { agent: ... }` field on plugin manifest, parsed by overlay crate.
- Subagent-config-time scope filter via override-layer injection at `build_agent_shared_config`.
- `agent-spawner` built-in role + Rust-native `spawn_top_level_session` function tool that routes through the Happy daemon HTTP control endpoint.
- Gate on subagent `spawn_agent` exposure in both v1/v2 paths (subagents cannot spawn further subagents).
- Tests: Rust unit tests in overlay crate (parser/predicate/filter); Rust integration tests in `multi_agents_tests.rs`; invariant test for source-pattern guard; vitest tests in happy-cli.
- Happy CLI daemon/control env plumbing for `HAPPY_CURRENT_SESSION_ID`, `HAPPY_DAEMON_CONTROL_URL`, and `/spawn-session-from-session` HTTP endpoint.
- Cross-package typecheck green for happy-cli / happy-server / happy-app / happy-wire.
- Rust CI green (via `codex/.github/workflows/invariant-check.yml`).
- Local fixture plugin (`packages/codexu-plugin`) declares `scope.agent: "both"`; test-only `top-level` fixture under `core/src/tools/handlers/multi_agents_tests/fixtures/`.
- Patch-surface documentation updates (in §14 + §15, not §17).

### Out of Scope
- Phase 2c `scope=host|agent|both` axis (not shipping yet; tracked separately in roadmap).
- Cross-repo update to `ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/ralph-orchestration/.codex-plugin/plugin.json` declaring `scope.agent: "top-level"`. Acceptance criterion is satisfied by a local-fixture test plugin instead.
- Surfacing `scope.agent` field to mobile UI (`happy-wire`/`happy-server`/`happy-app`). Scope-aware filtering is server-side only for this job.
- Marketplace cache propagation tooling (operators can reinstall manually).
- Migrating existing plugins to declare an explicit scope (default `Both` preserves visibility).
- Threading a `PluginLoadContext` parameter through `PluginsManager::plugins_for_config()` or `Config::to_mcp_config` (Option B). The single-seam Option A design makes this unnecessary.

## Risk Areas

1. **Non-spawn subagent paths (LOW):** If a future code change creates a subagent-context Session WITHOUT going through `build_agent_shared_config`, the filter is bypassed. **Mitigation:** the invariant test in `codex-rs-overlay/codex-invariant-tests/tests/plugin_scope_filtering.rs` source-pattern-grep asserts that the marker + filter call exist in `multi_agents_common.rs`, AND asserts that no `*.rs` under `core/src/tools/handlers/multi_agents*` performs `config.clone()` on a parent Config outside `build_agent_shared_config` / `build_agent_resume_config`. Implementer re-runs the inventory `git grep -n 'config.clone()' -- core/src/tools/handlers/multi_agents*/` at US-002 time and asserts coverage.
2. **Override-layer precedence (LOW):** The synthetic disable layer must beat user/project layers that might re-enable a plugin. **Mitigation:** US-002 has a precedence-stress integration test (parent config sets `[plugins.x] enabled = true`, subagent override forces `enabled = false`).
3. **Rebase drift on the single seam (MEDIUM):** Upstream changes to `build_agent_shared_config` may collide with the 3-to-5 line filter call. **Mitigation:** `// SANDBOX PATCH: plugin-scope-axis` marker + invariant test source-pattern check. The seam pattern is identical to `apply_spawn_agent_overrides`/`apply_spawn_agent_runtime_overrides` which have rebased cleanly multiple times. Register in `codex/docs/implementation/patch-surface.md` §14 + §15.
4. **agent-spawner privilege escalation (MEDIUM):** A subagent could attempt to invoke `spawn_top_level_session` to escape its sandbox. Mitigation: (a) native tool exposed only when `turn.session_source` is a subagent with role `agent-spawner`, (b) handler defensively checks role/source and requires `HAPPY_CURRENT_SESSION_ID`, (c) Happy daemon HTTP endpoint already relies on operator-side daemon trust. Log every spawn with audit fields.
5. **Marketplace cache divergence (LOW for this job):** Editing source `plugin.json` doesn't update cached installs. Mitigation: integration test loads the test fixture from the source path under `multi_agents_tests/fixtures/`, not from a cached install. Cross-repo ralph-orchestration manifest update tracked separately.
6. **Rust CI flake / slow signal (LOW):** No local cargo means feedback is push-and-wait. Mitigation: tight overlay-crate unit tests cover parser/predicate/filter logic with no Rust-toolchain risk on the Windows workstation; integration tests in `multi_agents_tests.rs` stay focused on the single scope-filter surface to keep CI cycles short.
7. **Manifest-cache staleness across plugin reinstall (LOW):** Operator reinstalls a plugin in a long-running codex process; cache still serves the pre-reinstall manifest. **Mitigation:** documented as expected behavior (matches today's plugin-cache semantics). Operator restarts codex to refresh. No reactive invalidation is in scope.

(Risks formerly listed in the original plan — H-1 "Scope filter bypass via cached outcome" and M-2 "Scope filter bypass via MCP forwarding" — are **dropped**. They are inapplicable to Option A: the manager cache key naturally differs for the subagent's mutated layer stack, and the subagent's Config never sees the top-level plugin's MCP servers because `to_mcp_config` iterates over the subagent-filtered `PluginLoadOutcome` produced by the unchanged manager.)

## Preliminary Story Decomposition

Net: **7 stories** (Option A collapse of US-002+US-003; everything else renumbered).

- **US-001: Scaffold `codex-plugin-scope` overlay crate.** Create the Cargo.toml + src/{lib,parser,context,predicate,filter}.rs + unit tests. Parser implements process-lifetime cache. `apply_subagent_plugin_filter(&mut Config)` synthesizes override layer. Register in workspace Cargo.toml + `core/Cargo.toml`. (small)
- **US-002: Subagent-config filter seam.** Edit `core/src/tools/handlers/multi_agents_common.rs::build_agent_shared_config` to call `codex_plugin_scope::apply_subagent_plugin_filter(&mut config)` AFTER `apply_spawn_agent_runtime_overrides`, gated behind `// SANDBOX PATCH: plugin-scope-axis` marker. Re-run the `git grep` inventory of `config.clone()` inside `multi_agents*` and `build_agent_*config` callers; document coverage in story log. Add integration test in `core/src/tools/handlers/multi_agents_tests.rs` (basic + precedence-stress). Add test fixture `multi_agents_tests/fixtures/top_level_only_plugin/.codex-plugin/plugin.json`. (small) Depends on US-001. **REPLACES the old US-002 (manager filtering seam) + old US-003 (call-site inventory + context plumbing) entirely. No `PluginLoadContext` signature threading. No `to_mcp_config` callers touched.**
- **US-003: `agent-spawner` role + Rust-native `spawn_top_level_session` contract/tool.** Register role in `core/src/agent/role.rs` (with the unit test asserting non-empty description); define the daemon HTTP request/response contract before implementing the handler; expose the tool from `tools/src/tool_config.rs` only for `SessionSource::SubAgent(... agent_role: Some("agent-spawner") ...)`; register in `core/src/tools/spec_plan.rs`; implement handler in `core/src/tools/handlers/spawn_top_level_session.rs`. (medium) Depends on US-001. **Lands co-resident with US-004 in the SAME commit** to avoid a transient window where subagents see `agent-spawner` exposure while still able to call `spawn_agent` (F-017).
- **US-004: Subagent `spawn_agent` gating.** Edit `tool_config.rs` + `core/src/tools/spec_plan.rs` to gate `spawn_agent` exposure on top-level context; add defensive rejects in both `multi_agents/spawn.rs` and `multi_agents_v2/spawn.rs`. Add one unit test per handler path. (small) **Same commit as US-003 (F-017).**
- **US-005: happy-cli daemon HTTP endpoint + env plumbing.** Implement the daemon side of US-003's Rust-native HTTP contract: add `/spawn-session-from-session` to `packages/happy-cli/src/daemon/controlServer.ts`, pass the existing handler from `daemon/run.ts`, and update `runCodex.ts` / `codexAppServerClient.ts` to inject `HAPPY_CURRENT_SESSION_ID` and `HAPPY_DAEMON_CONTROL_URL` into Codex app-server. Add vitest coverage for the route and env injection. (small) Depends on US-003.
- **US-006: Invariant test + patch-surface docs.** Add `codex-rs-overlay/codex-invariant-tests/tests/plugin_scope_filtering.rs` with marker assertions + non-spawn-path source-pattern guard. Register patches in `codex/docs/implementation/patch-surface.md` §14 + §15 (NOT §17). Update `plans/agent-view-research.md` "Status" footer. Update `plans/codexu-roadmap.md` follow-ups. (small) Depends on US-002, US-003, US-004, US-005.
- **US-007: Local fixture plugin + cross-package typecheck.** Set `scope.agent: "both"` in `packages/codexu-plugin/.codex-plugin/plugin.json`. Run `pnpm -r typecheck` to confirm green across happy-cli/happy-server/happy-app/happy-wire. (small) Depends on US-005.

## Suggested Decomposition

This work is intentionally serial. With Option A there is no file-overlap on `PluginsManager` or `Session::*` between stories, but US-003+US-004 must co-locate per F-017 and US-002 depends on US-001's overlay-crate API. Parallel decomposition is not recommended for the first ship.

### Cluster: rust-scope-machinery
- Stories: US-001, US-002, US-006
- Phase: 1
- Depends on: None
- File-overlap evidence: shared=[`codex/codex-rs-overlay/codex-plugin-scope/**` (US-001 only), `core/src/tools/handlers/multi_agents_common.rs` (US-002 only)]; exclusive=[overlay crate, `multi_agents_tests.rs`, invariant test]; risk=low
- `execution_mode` rationale: US-002 depends on US-001's `apply_subagent_plugin_filter` API. US-006 needs the seam files from US-002 to grep for markers. Serialize.

### Cluster: agent-spawner-and-daemon-rpc
- Stories: US-003, US-004, US-005
- Phase: 2
- Depends on: rust-scope-machinery
- File-overlap evidence: shared=[`tools/src/tool_config.rs`, `core/src/tools/spec_plan.rs` (US-003 + US-004 both edit these)]; exclusive=[`core/src/agent/role.rs`, `core/src/tools/handlers/spawn_top_level_session.rs`, `multi_agents/spawn.rs`, `multi_agents_v2/spawn.rs`, all happy-cli TS files]; risk=medium
- `execution_mode` rationale: US-003 + US-004 land in the same commit per F-017. US-005 depends on US-003's HTTP contract being settled. Serialize.

### Cluster: docs-and-fixtures
- Stories: US-007
- Phase: 3
- Depends on: agent-spawner-and-daemon-rpc
- File-overlap evidence: shared=[]; exclusive=[`packages/codexu-plugin/.codex-plugin/plugin.json`]; risk=low
- `execution_mode` rationale: Documentation and fixture closure. Trivial; keep in a single story.

Parallel handoff: `/implement-with-ralph --from-plan <plan_job_dir>/plan.md --parallel --suggested-decomposition <plan_job_dir>/suggested-decomposition.json` — **NOT RECOMMENDED for the first ship**; serial is simpler given the single-seam structure of Option A.

If an implementer-time discovery contradicts the above (e.g., `build_agent_shared_config` is NOT exhaustive, or override-layer precedence does NOT beat user-layer `enabled = true`), the implementer **must** report `kind=question` and pause — do not silently rework the design.
